objects.description: Boolean-like integral type used throughout FriBidi. Backed by int; nonzero typically means true, zero means false. No additional semantics specified here.
Unsigned 32-bit codepoint type representing a Unicode scalar value used by FriBidi APIs.
Signed integer index type for addressing positions within FriBidi strings or buffers. Size and sign follow the platform int.

objects.definition:
/* The MSB is used to indicate an opening bracket */
typedef FriBidiChar FriBidiBracketType;
objects.description: Bracket classification code stored in a 32-bit value (same representation as FriBidiChar). The most-significant bit indicates an opening bracket per the comment; FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET (0) denotes non-bracket. Further value semantics are not defined in this header.
Bitmask type for FriBidi option flags. Values are OR-ed combinations of FRIBIDI_FLAG_* macros controlling shaping, reordering, and removal behaviors. Underlying type is 32-bit unsigned integer.

Enumeration of joining types used for Arabic shaping, populated via macro inclusion. In normal (non-__FRIBIDI_DOC) builds, the public type FriBidiJoiningType is typedef’d to uint8_t instead of the enum, but the enum constants (FRIBIDI_JOINING_TYPE_*) exist. Used by API to represent per-character joining class. The actual enumerators are generated from fribidi-joining-types-list.h and map to bitmask-based *_VAL values defined in this header. Details like exact set of symbols depend on the included list header.

8-bit property type representing Arabic joining/shaping properties. Semantically similar to FriBidiJoiningType but not restricted to just the primary joining class values; it can carry additional bit flags (e.g., transparency, ignored, shaping).

Public type used by the API to carry a character’s joining class. In normal builds it is an 8-bit integer containing bitmask flags as defined by FRIBIDI_MASK_* and the *_VAL macros; in documentation builds it aliases the internal enum. Values are obtained via fribidi_get_joining_type or fribidi_get_joining_types.
Logical embedding level used by the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm. Stored as a signed 8-bit integer; even levels are LTR, odd levels are RTL.

objects.definition:
#if defined(__FRIBIDI_DOC) || (FRIBIDI_SIZEOF_INT+0 == 4 && !defined(__cplusplus))

typedef enum
{
# define _FRIBIDI_ADD_TYPE(TYPE,SYMBOL) \
	FRIBIDI_TYPE_##TYPE = FRIBIDI_TYPE_##TYPE##_VAL,
# include "fribidi-bidi-types-list.h"
# undef _FRIBIDI_ADD_TYPE
  _FRIBIDI_TYPE_SENTINEL = FRIBIDI_TYPE_SENTINEL	/* Don't use this */
} FriBidiCharType;

#else

typedef uint32_t FriBidiCharType;
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_LTR	FRIBIDI_TYPE_LTR_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_RTL	FRIBIDI_TYPE_RTL_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_AL	FRIBIDI_TYPE_AL_VAL

# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_AN	FRIBIDI_TYPE_AN_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_ES	FRIBIDI_TYPE_ES_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_ET	FRIBIDI_TYPE_ET_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_CS	FRIBIDI_TYPE_CS_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_NSM	FRIBIDI_TYPE_NSM_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_BN	FRIBIDI_TYPE_BN_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_BS	FRIBIDI_TYPE_BS_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_SS	FRIBIDI_TYPE_SS_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_WS	FRIBIDI_TYPE_WS_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_ON	FRIBIDI_TYPE_ON_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_LRE	FRIBIDI_TYPE_LRE_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_RLE	FRIBIDI_TYPE_RLE_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_LRO	FRIBIDI_TYPE_LRO_VAL

# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_LRI	FRIBIDI_TYPE_LRI_VAL

# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_FSI	FRIBIDI_TYPE_FSI_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_TYPE_PDI	FRIBIDI_TYPE_PDI_VAL
#endif
objects.description: Represents the bidi class of a character (e.g., LTR, RTL, AL, EN, etc.). Depending on platform/configuration it is either an enum (when sizeof(int)==4 and not C++) or a 32-bit unsigned integer. The specific constants map to bitmask combinations defined in this header.

objects.definition:
#if defined(__FRIBIDI_DOC) || (FRIBIDI_SIZEOF_INT+0 == 4 && !defined(__cplusplus))

typedef enum
{
# define _FRIBIDI_PAR_TYPES
# define _FRIBIDI_ADD_TYPE(TYPE,SYMBOL) \
	FRIBIDI_PAR_##TYPE = FRIBIDI_TYPE_##TYPE##_VAL,
# include "fribidi-bidi-types-list.h"
# undef _FRIBIDI_ADD_TYPE
# undef _FRIBIDI_PAR_TYPES
  _FRIBIDI_PAR_SENTINEL = FRIBIDI_TYPE_SENTINEL	/* Don't use this */
} FriBidiParType;

#else

typedef uint32_t FriBidiParType;
# define FRIBIDI_PAR_LTR	FRIBIDI_TYPE_LTR_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_PAR_RTL	FRIBIDI_TYPE_RTL_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_PAR_ON		FRIBIDI_TYPE_ON_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_PAR_WLTR	FRIBIDI_TYPE_WLTR_VAL
# define FRIBIDI_PAR_WRTL	FRIBIDI_TYPE_WRTL_VAL

#endif

/* Please don't use these two type names, use FRIBIDI_PAR_* form instead. */
#define FRIBIDI_TYPE_WLTR	FRIBIDI_PAR_WLTR
#define FRIBIDI_TYPE_WRTL	FRIBIDI_PAR_WRTL
objects.description: Paragraph direction type used to specify base direction or weak base direction (WLTR/WRTL). Like FriBidiCharType, it is an enum on some platforms and a 32-bit unsigned integer otherwise. Macros alias FRIBIDI_TYPE_WLTR/WRTL to the corresponding FRIBIDI_PAR_* values.
Paragraph base direction type used by FriBidi APIs. Not defined in this header; it is referenced to represent LTR, RTL, or neutral (ON) paragraph direction.
Bidi class/type per character as produced by fribidi_get_bidi_types(); referenced here for inputs to bidi processing. Defined elsewhere.
Bracket pairing/classification type used by the Unicode bidi algorithm for bracket processing; referenced here. Defined elsewhere.
Embedding level type (often an unsigned 8-bit integral type) used to store bidi levels. Referenced here as inputs/outputs of API; defined elsewhere.
String index type used by FriBidi to index into strings. Referenced for lengths, offsets, and maps; defined elsewhere.
Bitmask flags type controlling reordering behavior (e.g., FRIBIDI_FLAG_REORDER_NSM). Referenced here; definition resides in included headers.
Unicode scalar value/storage unit type used by FriBidi for character data and visual strings. Referenced here; defined elsewhere.

Bracket property bitfield/type used by FriBidi to encode whether a character is a bracket and, if so, its bracket id and whether it is an opening bracket. It is referenced here via function parameters/returns and associated macros, but its actual definition is not present in this header (likely defined in fribidi-bidi-types.h).
Code point type for Unicode characters used by FriBidi. Only referenced here as input/output character values; the definition is not present in this header (likely in fribidi-types.h).
String index/length integral type used by FriBidi for sizes and indices. Only referenced here; the definition is not present in this header.
Bidi character type enumeration used by FriBidi. Referenced as an input array describing bidi classes for each character; definition is external to this header.

No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It contains only macro-conditionally expanded invocations of _FRIBIDI_ADD_CHAR_SET_* macros to list character sets. Therefore, there are no custom data types introduced by this file.

Enumeration of supported character sets for FriBidi charset conversion. The actual members (FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_*) are injected by including fribidi-char-sets-list.h with a macro that expands to enum constants. The special values _FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_NOT_FOUND and _FRIBIDI_CHAR_SETS_NUM_PLUS_ONE mark an invalid/not-found value and a sentinel for the count, respectively. Macros provide FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_NOT_FOUND and FRIBIDI_CHAR_SETS_NUM as public aliases/count. Exact list of character sets is not present in this header and is included from another file.

Pointer to a NUL-terminated C string that reports the Unicode version implemented by FriBidi (format "x.y.z" or "unknown"). Although declared as a variable, it is a const char* type exposed by this header.

functions.name: fribidi_debug_status
functions.signature: int fribidi_debug_status(void);
functions.description: Returns the library’s current debug state as an integer. Intended for code that needs to query whether FriBidi’s internal debugging is enabled. Exact meaning and range of the returned value are not documented here; typically 0 means disabled and nonzero means enabled, but this is not explicitly stated.
requirements: Must be called in a context where the FriBidi library is available and properly linked.
No arguments are required; there are no documented preconditions beyond standard calling conventions.
Interpretation of the returned int is unspecified in this header; callers should be robust to any nonnegative/negative values unless library documentation specifies otherwise.

functions.name: fribidi_set_debug
functions.signature: int fribidi_set_debug(int state);
functions.description: Sets the library’s debug state to the provided integer value. Use to enable or disable FriBidi internal debugging/logging. The function returns an int (semantics not documented here; could represent the previous state or a status code—unknown).
requirements: Parameter state must be a valid int. Acceptable range/semantics are not specified in this header; callers should assume 0 disables and nonzero enables only if confirmed by external FriBidi documentation.
May be called whenever changing the debug setting is safe for your application; thread-safety and reentrancy are not documented here.
Callers should not rely on the return value’s specific meaning without consulting FriBidi’s full documentation; handle any int return value conservatively.

functions.name: fribidi_get_joining_type
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiJoiningType fribidi_get_joining_type(FriBidiChar ch) FRIBIDI_GNUC_CONST;
functions.description: Returns the Arabic joining type for a single Unicode character, as defined by Unicode’s Primary Arabic Joining Classes (Table 8-2), using data from ArabicShaping.txt and UnicodeData.txt. Typical use: call for each character to drive Arabic shaping/joining decisions or precompute character properties.
requirements: ch is a Unicode code point value stored in FriBidiChar (caller must ensure it is a valid code point as per library expectations; out-of-range handling is unspecified).
Function is declared FRIBIDI_GNUC_CONST: it has no side effects and its return depends only on input; it is safe to call repeatedly and usable in constant-folding contexts where applicable.

functions.name: fribidi_get_joining_types
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY void fribidi_get_joining_types(const FriBidiChar *str, const FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiJoiningType *jtypes);
functions.description: Computes Arabic joining types for a sequence of characters. It fills the output array jtypes with the joining type of each code point in str, analogous to calling fribidi_get_joining_type for each element.
requirements: str must point to an array of at least len elements of type FriBidiChar.
len specifies the number of characters to process; it must be non-negative and within the representable range of FriBidiStrIndex.
jtypes must point to an array with space for at least len elements of type FriBidiJoiningType; the function writes exactly len results.
The function does not allocate or free memory; the caller owns both input and output buffers.
Behavior for NULL pointers or mismatched buffer sizes is unspecified; callers must pass valid pointers when len > 0.

functions.name: fribidi_get_joining_type_name
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY const char *fribidi_get_joining_type_name(FriBidiJoiningType j) FRIBIDI_GNUC_CONST;
functions.description: Returns a human-readable, static C string naming the given joining type, matching the names in Unicode Table 8-2 Primary Arabic Joining Classes. Useful for debugging, logging, or UI display.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to a static string owned by the library; the caller must not modify or free it.
Valid inputs are FriBidiJoiningType values; handling of out-of-range/unknown values is not documented.
Function is FRIBIDI_GNUC_CONST: no side effects and result depends only on input.

functions.name: fribidi_join_arabic
functions.description: Applies the Unicode Arabic Cursive Joining algorithm (rules R1–R7) to compute per-character Arabic joining/shaping properties in-place. Given bidi types for a string, the paragraph embedding levels, and an array of Arabic properties initialized from joining types, the function updates ar_props to account for contextual joining behavior and bidi interaction. Typical usage: obtain bidi_types via fribidi_get_bidi_types(), embedding_levels via fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels(), initialize ar_props via fribidi_get_joining_types(), then call fribidi_join_arabic() before Arabic shaping/glyph selection. Details of internal errors are not reported (void return).
requirements: bidi_types must point to an array of at least len elements, each a FriBidiCharType corresponding to the same logical-order string, as returned by fribidi_get_bidi_types().
len specifies the number of characters to process and must match the lengths of bidi_types, embedding_levels, and ar_props arrays.
embedding_levels must point to an array of at least len FriBidiLevel values for the same string, as returned by fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels().
ar_props must point to a writable array of at least len FriBidiArabicProp entries initialized with joining types as returned by fribidi_get_joining_types().
All input arrays must refer to the same string segment and ordering (no mixing runs from different strings).
The function modifies ar_props in place; callers must preserve it if subsequent shaping requires the results.
The function does not return a status code; callers must ensure preconditions are met to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: fribidi_get_bidi_type
functions.signature: FriBidiCharType fribidi_get_bidi_type(FriBidiChar ch);
functions.description: Returns the Unicode Bidirectional (bidi) type of the given character, as defined by the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9). Typically used to precompute or inspect the bidi class for a single code point. The function is pure/const with respect to its input and does not depend on external state.
requirements: Input ch must be a valid FriBidiChar code point (typically a Unicode scalar value).
No error reporting: the function always returns a FriBidiCharType; caller should interpret the value using the FRIBIDI_TYPE_* constants and helper macros.

functions.name: fribidi_get_bidi_types
functions.signature: void fribidi_get_bidi_types(const FriBidiChar *str, FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiCharType *btypes);
functions.description: Computes the bidi type for each character in the input string and writes the results into the output array btypes. Use when you need the bidi class sequence for a buffer prior to running higher-level bidi processing.
requirements: If len > 0, str must be non-NULL and point to at least len elements of type FriBidiChar.
If len > 0, btypes must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for at least len elements of type FriBidiCharType.
len must be non-negative (FriBidiStrIndex length).
The function does not return an error code; caller must ensure buffer sizes are correct to avoid out-of-bounds access.

functions.name: fribidi_get_bidi_type_name
functions.signature: const char *fribidi_get_bidi_type_name(FriBidiCharType t);
functions.description: Returns the human-readable bidi type name for the given bidi type value (e.g., LTR, RTL, EN, AN). The returned pointer is a static string owned by the library; do not free it. Useful for diagnostics, logging, or debugging.
requirements: Input t should be a valid FriBidiCharType value (typically one of FRIBIDI_TYPE_* constants).
The returned string is static and must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Function is pure/const and has no side effects.

functions.name: fribidi_get_par_direction
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiParType fribidi_get_par_direction(const FriBidiCharType *bidi_types, const FriBidiStrIndex len);
functions.description: Determine the base (paragraph) direction according to Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm rule P2. Typically used when custom paragraph direction handling is needed; fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels() can compute base direction automatically. If multiple paragraphs are provided, returns the direction of the first non-neutral paragraph. Returns only LTR, RTL, or ON (no weak paragraph directions).
requirements: bidi_types must point to an array of FriBidiCharType of length len as produced by fribidi_get_bidi_types() for the same text.
len must match the number of elements available in bidi_types.
Function operates on paragraph-level data; if multiple paragraphs are included, result reflects the first non-neutral paragraph.
Return value is a FriBidiParType; callers should interpret only LTR, RTL, or ON as documented.

functions.name: fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiLevel fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex(const FriBidiCharType *bidi_types, const FriBidiBracketType *bracket_types, const FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiParType *pbase_dir, FriBidiLevel *embedding_levels) FRIBIDI_GNUC_WARN_UNUSED;
functions.description: Compute embedding levels for a single paragraph per the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (rules P2–I1 and parts 1–3 of L1; X9 handled by fribidi_remove_bidi_marks(), and part 4 of L1 by fribidi_reorder_line()). Use the macros in fribidi-bidi-types.h to inspect/manipulate levels. On success returns the maximum level found plus one; returns 0 on error (e.g., allocation failure). The paragraph base direction is provided via pbase_dir (requested) and resolved by the function.
requirements: bidi_types must point to an array of FriBidiCharType of length len as returned by fribidi_get_bidi_types() for the same paragraph text.
bracket_types must point to an array of FriBidiBracketType of length len as returned by fribidi_get_bracket_types() for the same text.
len must be the length (in code points) of the paragraph, matching both bidi_types and bracket_types.
pbase_dir must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a FriBidiParType; it provides the requested base direction and receives the resolved paragraph base direction.
embedding_levels must be a valid, writable array of FriBidiLevel with at least len elements to receive output levels.
Caller must check the return value; a return of 0 indicates an error (most likely memory allocation failure) and output contents should not be used.
This function processes exactly one paragraph; providing more than a paragraph is not supported by this API.

functions.name: fribidi_reorder_line
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiLevel fribidi_reorder_line(FriBidiFlags flags, const FriBidiCharType *bidi_types, const FriBidiStrIndex len, const FriBidiStrIndex off, const FriBidiParType base_dir, FriBidiLevel *embedding_levels, FriBidiChar *visual_str, FriBidiStrIndex *map) FRIBIDI_GNUC_WARN_UNUSED;
functions.description: Reorder a line from logical to visual order per UBA L1 (part 4), L2, and L3. Requires resolved paragraph direction and embedding levels (from fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels()). Trailing whitespace in the line has its level reset to the paragraph level (L1 part 4). The function can optionally reposition non-spacing marks in RTL runs after their base character when FRIBIDI_FLAG_REORDER_NSM is set (on by default via FRIBIDI_FLAGS_DEFAULT). Returns the maximum level found in the line plus one, or 0 on error. bidi_types and embedding_levels arrays themselves are not reordered; use the returned map to reorder other arrays as needed.
requirements: flags controls reordering behavior; FRIBIDI_FLAG_REORDER_NSM affects NSM placement. Use FRIBIDI_FLAGS_DEFAULT to enable typical behavior.
bidi_types must point to bidi types as returned by fribidi_get_bidi_types(); entries corresponding to the line segment [off, off+len) are used.
len is the length of the line segment to reorder and must match the number of elements available in visual_str (and, if provided, map).
off is the starting index of the line within the paragraph; it must correspond to the same paragraph used to compute embedding levels.
base_dir must be the resolved paragraph base direction for the paragraph containing the line.

embedding_levels must contain embedding levels as returned by fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels() for the paragraph; entries for the line [off, off+len) will be read and may be modified for trailing whitespace.
visual_str must be a writable buffer of FriBidiChar with at least len elements containing the logical-order text for the line; it will be reordered in place to visual order.

map may be NULL if no position mapping is needed; if non-NULL it must point to an array of FriBidiStrIndex with at least len elements and should be initialized by the caller to a sensible mapping (e.g., identity) before the call. The function updates it to reflect glyph positions after reordering.
Caller must check the return value; a return of 0 indicates an error (e.g., memory allocation failure) and results should not be used.

functions.name: fribidi_get_bracket
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiBracketType fribidi_get_bracket ( FriBidiChar ch );
functions.description: Returns the bracket type for the given character ch as defined by Unicode BidiBrackets.txt, and can be tested with FRIBIDI_IS_BRACKET. If ch is a bracket character with a paired counterpart, the paired character is conceptually identified and encoded in the returned type (use FRIBIDI_BRACKET_ID and FRIBIDI_IS_BRACKET_OPEN to inspect). Intended for use when processing bidirectional text to identify bracket pairing behavior. Details of exact encoding are per FriBidi’s bracket type definitions; use the provided macros to interpret.
requirements: ch must be a valid FriBidiChar value (typically a Unicode code point).
Callers should interpret the return value using FRIBIDI_IS_BRACKET, FRIBIDI_IS_BRACKET_OPEN, and FRIBIDI_BRACKET_ID macros to determine validity, openness, and pair id.
No side effects or output parameters; function is pure and can be called for any single character.

functions.name: fribidi_get_bracket_types
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY void fribidi_get_bracket_types ( const FriBidiChar *str, const FriBidiStrIndex len, const FriBidiCharType *types, FriBidiBracketType *btypes );
functions.description: Computes bracket types for each character in the input string str of length len. For each position, determines the bracket pairing information as in fribidi_get_bracket() and writes it to the corresponding position in btypes. The types array provides the bidi character types for the input text and should align 1:1 with str. Use FRIBIDI_IS_BRACKET/FRIBIDI_BRACKET_ID/FRIBIDI_IS_BRACKET_OPEN on elements of btypes to interpret results. Intended for preprocessing steps in bidirectional text layout to handle bracket pairing.
requirements: str must point to an array of at least len elements of FriBidiChar.
len must be non-negative and represent the number of elements in str to process.
types must point to an array of at least len elements of FriBidiCharType; each element corresponds to the bidi type of the character at the same index in str.
btypes must point to an array of at least len elements of FriBidiBracketType; it is an output buffer that will be filled by the function.
Pointers (str, types, btypes) must be valid for read/write as appropriate for at least len elements; they must not be NULL when len > 0.

functions.name: fribidi_get_mirror_char
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY fribidi_boolean fribidi_get_mirror_char(FriBidiChar ch, FriBidiChar *mirrored_ch)
functions.description: Returns whether the given Unicode character has a mirrored counterpart per Unicode BidiMirroring.txt, and if so writes that mirrored character to mirrored_ch; otherwise writes the input character itself. Typical usage: pass a code point and a writable output pointer to obtain the mirrored character for characters that mirror in right-to-left contexts.
requirements: mirrored_ch must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage for one FriBidiChar.
ch must be a valid FriBidiChar value (typically a Unicode code point).
On return, check the fribidi_boolean result to know whether a distinct mirroring equivalent exists (true) or not (false; mirrored_ch will equal ch).

functions.name: fribidi_shape_mirroring
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY void fribidi_shape_mirroring(const FriBidiLevel *embedding_levels, const FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiChar *str)
functions.description: In-place mirroring shaping: replaces mirroring characters in the string with their mirrored equivalents for positions that are in right-to-left embeddings, implementing Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm rule L4. embedding_levels should be the per-character embedding levels as returned by fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels for the same string.
requirements: embedding_levels must point to an array of at least len elements, as returned by fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels for the corresponding text.
str must point to a writable array of at least len FriBidiChar elements; the function modifies the string in place.
len specifies the length of both embedding_levels and str and must be consistent for both arrays.
The function expects embedding_levels to correspond index-for-index with the characters in str (same ordering and length).

functions.name: fribidi_shape_arabic
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY void fribidi_shape_arabic(FriBidiFlags flags, const FriBidiLevel *embedding_levels, const FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiArabicProp *ar_props, FriBidiChar *str)
functions.description: Performs Arabic shaping on the given string in place, according to the provided shaping flags. Depending on flags, it can apply mirroring, map Arabic letters to presentation forms, form mandatory ligatures, and apply terminal-friendly shaping for grid consoles. The function also updates the Arabic joining properties alongside shaping. Usage: prepare the input text and its Arabic joining properties (via fribidi_join_arabic), compute embedding levels for the text (for correct mirroring behavior), then call this function with those arrays and desired flags. Note: Only shaping-related flags affect this routine; documented flags include FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_MIRRORING, FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_ARAB_PRES, FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_ARAB_LIGA, and FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_ARAB_CONSOLE. FRIBIDI_FLAGS_ARABIC is a convenient preset of recommended shaping flags.
requirements: flags: Should be a combination of shaping-related flags; only FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_MIRRORING and flags starting with FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_ARAB_* affect shaping in this function.

embedding_levels must point to an array of at least len elements, corresponding to the same text in str; levels should be computed for the same string segment to ensure correct mirroring behavior when FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_MIRRORING is used.
len must equal the number of code points available in str and the number of elements available in ar_props and embedding_levels for this call; must not exceed the allocated sizes of those arrays.
ar_props must point to an array of at least len elements containing Arabic properties as computed by fribidi_join_arabic for the same string segment; this array is used and may be updated in place.
str must point to a mutable buffer of at least len FriBidiChar elements; the content will be modified in place by shaping (e.g., presentation forms, ligatures, mirroring) depending on flags.
The function returns void and does not report errors; callers should not expect error codes or exceptions from this routine.

functions.name: fribidi_shape
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY void fribidi_shape(FriBidiFlags flags, const FriBidiLevel *embedding_levels, const FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiArabicProp *ar_props, FriBidiChar *str);
functions.description: Performs bidi-aware shaping on a string in place, applying mirroring and optionally Arabic shaping based on resolved embedding levels. It wraps fribidi_shape_mirroring and fribidi_shape_arabic. Use it after computing embedding levels (via fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels) and, if Arabic shaping is desired, after computing Arabic joining properties (via fribidi_join_arabic). The flags control which FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_* operations are applied; mirroring is enabled by default (FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_MIRRORING). If ar_props is NULL, Arabic shaping is skipped. The input string is an array of FriBidiChar code points and will be modified in place.
requirements: embedding_levels must point to an array of at least len elements containing the resolved embedding levels for str, as returned by fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels.
len must be the number of code points in str; it must be non-negative and consistent across embedding_levels, ar_props (if provided), and str.
str must point to a writable array of at least len FriBidiChar code points; contents will be modified in place by the function.
If Arabic shaping is desired, ar_props must point to a writable array of at least len elements, precomputed for the same string via fribidi_join_arabic; otherwise pass NULL to skip Arabic shaping.
flags should contain only relevant FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_* bits to affect shaping; FRIBIDI_FLAG_SHAPE_MIRRORING is enabled by default (FRIBIDI_FLAGS_DEFAULT).
Call this function only after computing embedding levels; otherwise behavior is undefined or incorrect.
Input string encoding must be in FriBidiChar units (Unicode scalar values/UCS-4 as defined by FriBidi), not UTF-8 bytes.
The function returns void and does not report errors; callers must ensure arguments meet the above requirements to avoid invalid memory access or incorrect shaping.

functions.name: fribidi_charset_to_unicode
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiStrIndex fribidi_charset_to_unicode ( FriBidiCharSet char_set, const char *s, FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiChar *us );
functions.description: Converts a byte string encoded in the specified legacy character set to a Unicode string (array of FriBidiChar). Returns the length of the converted Unicode string. Intended for preparing text for Unicode-based processing (e.g., bidi). The input buffer need not be null-terminated; length is provided explicitly. Details of substitution or error handling for unmappable bytes are not documented here.
requirements: char_set must be a valid FriBidiCharSet value; behavior is undefined/unknown if FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_NOT_FOUND is used.
s points to an input buffer of at least len bytes; s may be non-null even if len==0; if len>0, s must be non-null.

us points to an output buffer large enough to hold the resulting Unicode code points; exact maximum size is not documented. Based on typical single-byte charsets, allocating at least len FriBidiChar elements is generally sufficient; specifics for multi-byte encodings are unknown.
len specifies the number of input bytes to convert; it may be zero.
Return value is the length of the output written; callers should handle the returned length and must not assume null-termination of the Unicode output.
Error signaling (e.g., negative return on failure) is not documented; callers should treat nonnegative return as the count and any unexpected values conservatively (unknown).

functions.name: fribidi_unicode_to_charset
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiStrIndex fribidi_unicode_to_charset ( FriBidiCharSet char_set, const FriBidiChar *us, FriBidiStrIndex len, char *s );
functions.description: Converts a Unicode string (array of FriBidiChar) to a string encoded in the specified legacy character set and null-terminates the output. Returns the length of the encoded (non-null-terminator) output string. Intended for producing text in a target charset after Unicode processing.
requirements: char_set must be a valid FriBidiCharSet value; behavior is undefined/unknown if FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_NOT_FOUND is used.
us points to an input array of at least len Unicode code points; if len>0, us must be non-null.

s points to an output buffer large enough for the encoded result plus a terminating null byte; exact maximum required size is not documented and depends on the charset. For single-byte charsets, allocating at least len+1 bytes is typically sufficient; specifics for other charsets are unknown.
len specifies the number of Unicode code points to convert; it may be zero.
The function will write a terminating '\0' to s; callers must not rely on any additional terminators.
Return value is the length of the output not counting the terminator; precise error signaling for unmappable code points is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: fribidi_parse_charset
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiCharSet fribidi_parse_charset ( const char *s );
functions.description: Parses a character set name string and returns the corresponding FriBidiCharSet enum value. Returns FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_NOT_FOUND if the named charset is not available. Useful for mapping user-supplied or configuration strings to the enum.
requirements: s must be a pointer to a null-terminated C string naming a character set; s must be non-null.
The mapping of names/aliases and case-sensitivity rules are not documented here (unknown).
Callers must handle the possibility of FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_NOT_FOUND being returned.

functions.name: fribidi_char_set_name
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY const char *fribidi_char_set_name ( FriBidiCharSet char_set );
functions.description: Returns a short name string for the specified character set. Intended for display or serialization. The returned pointer refers to an internal static string or constant; allocation/ownership details are not documented here.
requirements: char_set must be a valid FriBidiCharSet value in range [0, FRIBIDI_CHAR_SETS_NUM); behavior when passing FRIBIDI_CHAR_SET_NOT_FOUND or out-of-range values is not documented (unknown).
The returned pointer should be treated as read-only; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: fribidi_char_set_title
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY const char *fribidi_char_set_title ( FriBidiCharSet char_set );
functions.description: Returns a human-readable title for the specified character set. Useful for UI display. The returned pointer likely refers to a static read-only string; ownership details are not documented.
requirements: char_set must be a valid FriBidiCharSet value; behavior for invalid/out-of-range values is not documented (unknown).
The returned pointer is read-only and must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: fribidi_char_set_desc
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY const char *fribidi_char_set_desc ( FriBidiCharSet char_set );
functions.description: Returns a longer description string for the specified character set. Useful for help text or tooltips. The returned pointer is expected to be a static read-only string; exact ownership semantics are not documented.
requirements: char_set must be a valid FriBidiCharSet value; behavior for invalid/out-of-range values is not documented (unknown).
The returned pointer is read-only and must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: fribidi_remove_bidi_marks
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiStrIndex fribidi_remove_bidi_marks(FriBidiChar *str, const FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiStrIndex *positions_to_this, FriBidiStrIndex *position_from_this_list, FriBidiLevel *embedding_levels);
functions.description: Removes bidirectional and boundary-neutral marks from a string in place, implementing Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm rule X9 (also removes U+200E LRM and U+200F RLM). Optionally updates position-mapping arrays and embedding levels to reflect removed characters. Use when you need to strip bidi control marks from either the logical or visual string and keep mapping data coherent. If a map points to a removed character it will be set to −1. For best results, run on a full paragraph rather than individual lines. Do not use embedding_levels if str is a visual string.
requirements: str must point to a mutable buffer of at least len FriBidiChar elements; the function compacts the string in place and returns the new length (<= len).
len must be the number of code units in str to process (non-negative).
positions_to_this may be NULL; if non-NULL it must reference an array of at least len FriBidiStrIndex entries already filled with valid mappings for the current order of str.
position_from_this_list may be NULL; if non-NULL it must reference an array of at least len FriBidiStrIndex entries already filled with valid mappings for the current order of str.

If str is the visual string, positions_to_this must be the logical-to-visual map (positions_L_to_V) and position_from_this_list must be the visual-to-logical map (positions_V_to_L). If str is the logical string, the opposite applies.
If a position map entry corresponds to a removed character, that entry will be set to -1; callers must be prepared to handle -1 values.
embedding_levels may be NULL; if non-NULL it must reference an array of at least len FriBidiLevel entries corresponding to str; embedding_levels should not be used when str is the visual string.
On error, the function returns -1; callers must check the return value and avoid using outputs if an error is reported.
For most accurate results, call on entire paragraphs rather than broken lines.

functions.name: fribidi_log2vis
functions.signature: FRIBIDI_ENTRY FriBidiLevel fribidi_log2vis(const FriBidiChar *str, const FriBidiStrIndex len, FriBidiParType *pbase_dir, FriBidiChar *visual_str, FriBidiStrIndex *positions_L_to_V, FriBidiStrIndex *positions_V_to_L, FriBidiLevel *embedding_levels);
functions.description: Converts a logical-order Unicode string to visual order according to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm. Optionally produces logical-to-visual and visual-to-logical position maps and per-character embedding levels. pbase_dir is both input (requested paragraph base direction) and output (resolved paragraph base direction). Intended for one-line paragraphs; for multi-paragraph text, split input into paragraphs and carry the resolved pbase_dir between calls. Returns the maximum embedding level found plus one; returns 0 on failure.
requirements: str must point to a buffer containing at least len FriBidiChar code units; it is read-only to this function.
len must be the number of code units in str to process (non-negative).
pbase_dir must be non-NULL and point to a valid FriBidiParType value; on return it holds the resolved base direction for the paragraph.
visual_str must point to a writable buffer with capacity for at least len FriBidiChar elements to receive the visual-order string.
positions_L_to_V may be NULL; if non-NULL it must reference an array of at least len FriBidiStrIndex entries to receive logical-to-visual position mapping.
positions_V_to_L may be NULL; if non-NULL it must reference an array of at least len FriBidiStrIndex entries to receive visual-to-logical position mapping.
embedding_levels may be NULL; if non-NULL it must reference an array of at least len FriBidiLevel entries to receive per-character levels.
The function is designed for one-line paragraphs; for multi-paragraph text, callers must split into paragraphs and carry over the resolved pbase_dir for subsequent lines.
On success, the return value is max_level + 1; on error, the function returns 0. Callers must check for a 0 return and handle it as failure (e.g., due to memory allocation).

data_types.description: An unconstrained byte string used as raw entropy. The stub interprets the bytes in various ways: assembling 32-bit integers to form Unicode code points, treating bytes directly as small code points, or filling arrays of small integers (levels, properties). No specific encoding or structure is required; any sequence of bytes of arbitrary length is valid.

A human-readable charset identifier passed as a null-terminated C string to fribidi_parse_charset (e.g., "ISO-8859-6", "windows-1256", "UTF-8"). Case and alias handling are library-defined. Used to select a FriBidiCharSet; invalid names may map to NOT_FOUND.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces arbitrary binary data tailored to FriBidi fuzz stubs that
# consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as entropy to build Unicode codepoints, levels, properties,
# and charset names. We synthesize a mix of bytes that include:
# - ASCII LTR letters (English), RTL letters (Arabic/Hebrew), digits, punctuation,
# - Brackets and mirrored characters to exercise bracket/mirroring paths,
# - Bidi control marks (LRE/RLE/LRO/RLO/PDF/LRI/RLI/FSI/PDI, LRM/RLM) to exercise X9 removal,
# - UTF-8-like multi-byte sequences (though stubs treat bytes as raw),
# - Repeated patterns and varied lengths to ensure enough 4-byte chunks for codepoints.
# The stubs typically slice the FUZZ_PARAM_STR into 1..4096 bytes. We keep <=4096.

BIDI_CONTROLS = [
    0xE2, 0x80, 0xAA,  # U+202A LRE (UTF-8)
    0xE2, 0x80, 0xAB,  # U+202B RLE
    0xE2, 0x80, 0xA9,  # U+2029 PS (paragraph sep)
    0xE2, 0x80, 0xA8,  # U+2028 LS (line sep)
    0xE2, 0x80, 0xAC,  # U+202C PDF
    0xE2, 0x80, 0xAD,  # U+202D LRO
    0xE2, 0x80, 0xAE,  # U+202E RLO
    0xE2, 0x81, 0xA6,  # U+2066 LRI
    0xE2, 0x81, 0xA7,  # U+2067 RLI
    0xE2, 0x81, 0xA9,  # U+2069 PDI
    0xE2, 0x80, 0x8E,  # U+200E LRM
    0xE2, 0x80, 0x8F,  # U+200F RLM
]

BRACKETS_ASCII = list(b"()[]{}<>")
MIRRORABLE_UTF8 = [
    # U+00AB «, U+00BB », U+2039 ‹, U+203A ›
    0xC2, 0xAB, 0xC2, 0xBB, 0xE2, 0x80, 0xB9, 0xE2, 0x80, 0xBA,
]

# Some Hebrew and Arabic bytes (UTF-8 sequences) to induce RTL classes
HEBREW_UTF8 = [
    0xD7, 0x90, 0xD7, 0xA9, 0xD7, 0x9C, 0xD7, 0x95, 0xD7, 0x9D  # אשלום (parts of "שלום")
]
ARABIC_UTF8 = [
    0xD8, 0xA7, 0xD9, 0x84, 0xD8, 0xB3, 0xD9, 0x84, 0xD8, 0xA7, 0xD9, 0x85  # السلام
]

DIGITS = list(b"0123456789")
ASCII_LETTERS = list(b"The quick brown fox jumps over 13 lazy dogs. ")
PUNCT = list(b".,;:!?/|\\\"'@#$%^&*-_=+`~")

# Charset names and aliases likely recognized by fribidi_parse_charset
CHARSETS = [
    b"UTF-8", b"ISO-8859-6", b"ISO-8859-8", b"CP1256", b"WINDOWS-1256", b"CP1255",
    b"WINDOWS-1255", b"ISO-8859-1", b"KOI8-R", b"MACARABIC", b"IBM864", b"IBM862"
]

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _build_mix(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytearray:
    out = bytearray()
    # Start with a charset name to help charset stubs get a valid value
    cs = rng.choice(CHARSETS)
    out += cs + b"\n"

    # Add patterns ensuring enough bytes for 4-byte codepoint assembly
    components: List[bytes] = []
    components.append(bytes(ASCII_LETTERS))
    components.append(bytes(DIGITS))
    components.append(bytes(PUNCT))
    components.append(bytes(BRACKETS_ASCII))
    components.append(bytes(BIDI_CONTROLS))
    components.append(bytes(MIRRORABLE_UTF8))
    components.append(bytes(HEBREW_UTF8))
    components.append(bytes(ARABIC_UTF8))

    # Shuffle and repeat components
    rng.shuffle(components)
    for chunk in components:
        out += chunk
        if len(out) >= target_len:
            return out[:target_len]

    # Pad with structured 4-byte little-endian values in Unicode range
    while len(out) < target_len:
        # Compose a codepoint avoiding surrogates
        cp = rng.randrange(0x110000)
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            cp = 0xE000 + (cp - 0xD800) % (0xF900 - 0xE000)
        out += struct.pack('<I', cp)
    return out[:target_len]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a size that covers common stub caps; ensure divisible by 4 sometimes
    base_len = rng.randint(64, 1024)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base_len = (base_len // 4) * 4
    # Occasionally produce a larger blob to feed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base_len = min(2048, base_len + rng.randint(0, 1024))

    data = _build_mix(rng, base_len)

    # Optionally append another charset name and more control/brackets to enrich later slices
    if len(data) + 64 <= 4096 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        data += b"\n" + rng.choice(CHARSETS) + b"\n"
        data += bytes(BIDI_CONTROLS)
        data += bytes(BRACKETS_ASCII)

    # Ensure non-empty and <= 4096
    if not data:
        data = b"A"
    return bytes(data[:4096])

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces a bytes buffer intended to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# in the provided stubs. The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times to obtain:
# 1) legacy-encoded byte buffers (arbitrary bytes, length capped to 1024 by stub), and
# 2) character set name strings to feed fribidi_parse_charset.
#
# We therefore craft a single bytes blob that concatenates multiple C-strings
# (null-terminated) so that different FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can draw meaningful
# slices from the same buffer: a mix of valid and interesting charset names,
# plus some arbitrary byte buffers that include edge cases (NULs, high-bytes, etc.).
#
# Design:
# - Emit a sequence of NUL-terminated strings.
# - Include multiple well-known charset names and common aliases that FriBidi
#   is likely to recognize, covering Arabic-relevant encodings and others.
# - Include variations in case and with/without dashes to exercise aliasing.
# - Include some invalid/unknown names to exercise NOT_FOUND paths (the stub
#   will bail when necessary, but other stubs just parse and continue).
# - Include raw byte payload strings for the legacy input buffers used by
#   fribidi_charset_to_unicode and for the seed used by fribidi_unicode_to_charset.
#   These payloads are also NUL-terminated C-strings but may embed binary bytes
#   before the NUL. The stub uses std::string which can hold NULs.
#
# Buffer size is kept <= 4096 bytes.

KNOWN_CHARSETS = [
    # UTF encodings
    "UTF-8", "utf8", "Utf-8",
    "UTF-16", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-16LE",
    # ISO-8859 Arabic and related
    "ISO-8859-6", "iso8859-6", "ISO_8859-6",
    # Windows code pages
    "windows-1256", "cp1256", "Windows-1256",
    # Hebrew (directionality interactions)
    "ISO-8859-8", "windows-1255",
    # Latin
    "ISO-8859-1", "windows-1252", "cp1252",
    # Mac and KOI
    "MacArabic", "KOI8-R",
    # IBM code pages
    "IBM864", "cp864",
]

INVALID_CHARSETS = [
    "UTF-80", "latin-0", "cp12x", "unknown", "", "--", "1256win",
]

# Some short Arabic text snippets in various encodings for legacy buffers
# We generate bytes procedurally as we cannot rely on external codecs; we just
# craft representative byte patterns. The stub treats them as opaque bytes.

def _mk_legacy_bytes_arabic(seed: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a mixture of plausible single-byte Arabic code page bytes
    # Windows-1256 Arabic letters roughly 0xC7..0xFF with gaps; we sample high bytes.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Include ASCII with punctuation and brackets for mirroring/bracket logic upstream
    ascii_prefix = b"Hello (World)! [Test] {Sample} <> \t\n"
    parts.append(ascii_prefix)
    # Add a run of high bytes
    high = bytes(seed.randrange(0xC0, 0xFF) for _ in range(seed.randint(8, 32)))
    parts.append(high)
    # Add zeros inside to test embedded NUL handling
    if seed.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(b"\x00")
        parts.append(bytes(seed.randrange(0x80, 0xC0) for _ in range(seed.randint(4, 16))))
    # Add some digits and punctuation to mix bidi classes
    parts.append(b" 12345 +-/,:.;? ")
    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > max_len:
        data = data[:max_len]
    return data


def _mk_binary_blob(seed: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Arbitrary bytes including control chars and high bytes
    n = seed.randint(0, max_len)
    return bytes(seed.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))


def _random_charset_name(seed: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose among known valid names with high probability to satisfy stubs
    # that require a valid charset; occasionally produce invalid to exercise parser.
    if seed.random() < 0.8:
        base = seed.choice(KNOWN_CHARSETS)
    else:
        base = seed.choice(INVALID_CHARSETS)
    # Random case mangling and optional whitespace trimming
    style = seed.randint(0, 3)
    if style == 1:
        base = base.lower()
    elif style == 2:
        base = base.upper()
    elif style == 3:
        base = base.title()
    # Sometimes add aliases like removing dashes
    if seed.random() < 0.3 and base:
        base = base.replace("-", "")
    # Sometimes add surrounding spaces (parser should handle/ignore or fail)
    if seed.random() < 0.2:
        base = (" " * seed.randint(0, 2)) + base + (" " * seed.randint(0, 2))
    return base


def _cstr(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure exactly one terminating NUL; if b already contains NULs inside, keep them
    return b + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Provide several valid charset names early to satisfy stubs that bail on NOT_FOUND
    num_valid = rng.randint(3, 6)
    picked_valid = rng.sample(KNOWN_CHARSETS, k=min(num_valid, len(KNOWN_CHARSETS)))
    for name in picked_valid:
        # Randomly transform case/format via helper for diversity but keep valid pool
        rng2 = random.Random(rng.getrandbits(32))
        styled = name
        style = rng2.randint(0, 2)
        if style == 1:
            styled = name.lower()
        elif style == 2:
            styled = name.upper()
        # Occasionally strip dashes for alias forms
        if rng2.random() < 0.3:
            styled = styled.replace("-", "")
        chunks.append(_cstr(styled.encode('ascii', 'ignore')))

    # 2) Add some random charset names (valid or invalid) for the pure parser fuzzer
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        s = _random_charset_name(rng)
        # Try ascii encoding; fallback to replacing with '?'
        chunks.append(_cstr(s.encode('ascii', 'replace')))

    # 3) Add legacy byte buffers for fribidi_charset_to_unicode
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        payload = _mk_legacy_bytes_arabic(rng, 1024)
        chunks.append(_cstr(payload))

    # 4) Add seed buffers for fribidi_unicode_to_charset (arbitrary bytes ok)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        payload = _mk_binary_blob(rng, 1024)
        chunks.append(_cstr(payload))

    # 5) Ensure at least one tiny and one empty string
    chunks.append(_cstr(b""))
    chunks.append(_cstr(b"A"))

    blob = b"".join(chunks)

    # Enforce size limit <= 4096 bytes
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4095]  # leave room to append a final NUL
        # Ensure blob ends with NUL to keep last C-string terminated
        if not blob.endswith(b"\x00"):
            blob += b"\x00"

    return blob
